equipment.description: Standard centrifugal pump for moving treated water.
Pump submerged in water, commonly used in lift stations and deep wells.
Positive displacement pump for accurate chemical dosing (e.g., chlorine, coagulants).
Positive displacement pump used for moving highly viscous sludge.
High-capacity pump typically used for drawing water from deep wells or reservoirs.
Air-operated pump often used for abrasive or corrosive chemical transfer.
High-volume, low-head pump for raw water intake or stormwater pumping.
Positive displacement blower providing air to aeration basins.
High-speed blower used for continuous aeration in biological treatment.
High-efficiency gearless blower with air or magnetic bearings for aeration.
Compressor providing instrument air for pneumatic valves and controls.
Mixer installed underwater to prevent settling and maintain suspension.
Slow-moving mixer designed to promote agglomeration of flocs without shearing.
Inline device with motionless elements for rapid chemical mixing.
High-speed mixer for rapid, homogeneous dispersion of coagulants.
Large circular or rectangular tank for settling out suspended solids.
Basin where oxygen is introduced to promote biological breakdown of organic matter.
Sealed vessel for anaerobic decomposition of sludge, producing biogas.
Corrosion-resistant tank for storing treatment chemicals like sodium hypochlorite.
Basin with gentle mixing where coagulated particles form larger flocs.
Storage reservoir for finished, treated potable water before distribution.
Vessel absorbing pressure transients or water hammer in pumping systems.
Vessel containing layers of sand and gravel to remove particulate matter.
Pressure or gravity filter with multiple layers of media (anthracite, sand, garnet).
System utilizing semi-permeable membranes to remove dissolved salts and minerals.
Membrane filter removing suspended solids, bacteria, and large macromolecules.
Combination of a membrane process with a suspended growth bioreactor.
Mechanical screen removing large debris from raw influent.
Rotating drum screen with fine mesh for removing small suspended solids.
Chamber designed to slow flow and allow heavy inorganic grit to settle.
System using ultraviolet light to inactivate pathogenic microorganisms.
Electrical device generating ozone gas for strong oxidation and disinfection.
Baffled tank ensuring adequate contact time for chlorine disinfection.
Heat exchanger designed to preheat sludge before it enters a digester.
Linear motion valve for on-off service with minimal pressure drop.
Quarter-turn valve used for isolation or throttling in large water mains.
Valve permitting water flow in only one direction, preventing backflow.
Valve automatically releasing accumulated air pockets from pressurized pipelines.
Valve that automatically reduces higher inlet pressure to a steady lower downstream pressure.
Sliding gate mechanism used to control water flow in open channels or tanks.
Quarter-turn valve with a cylindrical or tapered plug, ideal for sludge.
Flow meter using electromagnetic induction to measure volumetric flow of conductive liquids.
Non-intrusive flow meter measuring fluid velocity using ultrasound waves.
Non-contact sensor measuring the distance to a liquid surface using sound waves.
High-accuracy sensor using microwave radar pulses to determine liquid level.
Device measuring fluid pressure in pipelines and tanks.
Measures the difference in pressure across a restriction or filter to determine flow or level.
Analytical probe measuring the acidity or alkalinity of the water.
Instrument measuring water clarity by the amount of light scattered by suspended particles.
Sensor measuring the amount of oxygen dissolved in aeration basins.
Continuous analyzer measuring the concentration of active chlorine remaining after disinfection.
Oxidation-Reduction Potential sensor used to monitor chemical reactions like chlorination.
Standard asynchronous electric motor used to drive pumps and blowers.
Electronic controller adjusting motor speed by varying frequency, optimizing energy use.
Assembly to control electric motors, containing starters, VFDs, and protection devices.
Electrical disconnect switches and circuit breakers protecting facility equipment.
Diesel or gas generator providing emergency power during grid outages.
